gating: Gated (Chapter 5 young-adult settings; comprehensive info is the norm)
note: STI/HIV testing & treatment, made personal and adult (UNESCO 8.2, 8.3). New v2 build, Chapter 5. Owning your sexual health: testing is power, not shame; build your prevention stack; talk to a partner; treatment works (HIV manageable, U=U undetectable=untransmittable; most STIs treatable, several curable); dignity for all, zero stigma. Comprehensive but never explicit; delaying respected. Builds on g23 (Outbreak); pairs g29; links g31 (Mutual). India: NACO ICTC free confidential testing, RKSK clinics, PrEP where available; POCSO-aware for under-18s; routes coercion/distress to help.

categories.know-your-status: Know your status: testing as self-care

evidenceBase: Testing is routine, empowering self-care, not an admission of guilt; you can't tell status by looking, and only testing tells you. HIV self-tests and rapid tests are reliable read after the window period (about 3 months for antibody/self-tests; lab and NAT tests detect sooner). In India, NACO Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres (ICTC, 4,400+) offer free, confidential HIV testing and counselling (WHO; NACO)

Treatment works: HIV is a manageable long-term condition, and effective treatment that keeps the virus undetectable means it cannot be sexually transmitted (U=U, undetectable = untransmittable, supported by studies showing zero transmissions from an undetectable partner). Most STIs are treatable and several (chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, trichomoniasis) are curable; a diagnosis is information to act on, not a verdict on a person (WHO; UNESCO KC8.2/8.3)

A comprehensive personal prevention 'stack' is layered and chosen: condoms (the only method that also prevents pregnancy), the HPV vaccine, PrEP where relevant (now including long-acting injectables such as cabotegravir and twice-yearly lenacapavir), regular testing and honest mutual disclosure; delaying remains fully respected. Dignity is non-negotiable: status is never linked to a person's character or group, and confidentiality and anti-stigma are paramount; for under-18s the law (POCSO) protects them and coercion routes to help (NACO; WHO; CDC)
